text:
The Panthers are 12-7-3 without Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand, and that is the headline of their season so far. Reports say both could be back within two weeks, which would turn a solid team into a scary one again.

What's carried them is the Tkachuk brothers. Brady and Matthew have played with Sam Bennett on Florida's most-used line, and it has taken 57% of the expected goals (the quality of chances). Saturday in St. Louis, on the night the Blues honoured their father Keith, both scored in a 4-1 win, and Matthew picked up his 700th point a day later in Dallas. The Eetu Luostarinen, Anton Lundell and Sandis Vilmanis line has been even better by the chances (63%) without the goals to show for it, and Lundell is running hot with 8 points in 10.

The team numbers are good, not dominant: 52.6% of the expected goals, 52% at five on five, and a power play that creates 1.08 expected goals a game, the best in this group. Florida has actually scored about four fewer goals than its chances deserve, so there's no luck to give back. The only odd note is the pace of penalties, 5.3 a game each way, which turns a lot of nights into special-teams contests.

Our simulations put them at 96 points and a 68% playoff chance. That number was built without Barkov and Marchand in the lineup.
